subject.title: [Bug]: Codex OAuth profile in main agentDir does not propagate to subagent sessions — silent fallback hallucinates tool calls in production

question: Should dynamic subagents inherit the main agent's Codex/OpenAI OAuth owner by default, and what should happen when that intended OAuth route is unavailable?
rationale: The source fixes and tests cover inherited OAuth pieces, but the remaining choice affects provider routing, fallback visibility, billing, security boundaries, and live scheduled/channel behavior.

options.title: Require inherited-owner live proof and loud fallback diagnostics
options.body: Accept main-agent OAuth read-through as the intended default, but keep this open until the exact spawned-subagent path is live-proven and auth-loss fallback emits an operator-visible warning or failure.

options.title: Fail closed on missing intended OAuth
options.body: Treat unavailable Codex OAuth as a hard subagent auth error before any alternate provider fallback can run, trading compatibility for clearer billing and security behavior.

options.title: Split fallback policy into a new canonical item
options.body: Close only after a narrower canonical issue owns fallback visibility and this issue has proof that auth inheritance itself works for spawned subagents.

recommendation.title: Require inherited-owner live proof and loud fallback diagnostics
recommendation.body: Accept main-agent OAuth read-through as the intended default, but keep this open until the exact spawned-subagent path is live-proven and auth-loss fallback emits an operator-visible warning or failure.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged history most directly covers Codex OAuth bridge security and canonical OAuth routing, which are the core decision surfaces here.
